text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Monthly inflation in Lithuania in October was 0.1 percent. The government's target for a 15 percent annual rate by the end of 1996 is on track.
- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas does not expect any conflict with the new parliament.
- Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Stankevicius has rejected Estonia's offer to act as a mediator in the sea border dispute between Latvia and Lithuania.
- The Bank of Lithuania approved the application of Poland's Kredyt Bank SA to open a branch in Vilnius. Kredyt Bank SA is the first foreign bank to enter Lithuania's banking market.
- Young Lithuanians often fake poor health to avoid military service. Only 3,363 out of a potential 7,483 conscripts were drafted into the army this fall.
- Lithuanians go the polls on Sunday for the second round of parlaimentary elections.
- Lithuanian new car sales dropped to 4,734 during the first nine months of 1996, a 16 percent fall on the corresponding period last year.
- Lithuanian Guns Merchants' association which unites 13 companies, protests against the government decision to grant the subordinate Weapons Fund a monopoly on weapons trade.
